business_problem: Paytm Mobile Solutions (Paytm) has a massive infrastructure and scales to accommodate millions of active users, so keeping costs down is vital. In 2021, Paytm decided to optimize its compute costs on AWS.
solution_summary: Paytm Mobile Solutions (Paytm) has a massive infrastructure and scales to accommodate millions of active users, so keeping costs down is vital. In 2021, Paytm decided to optimize its compute costs on AWS. Paytm first migrated its MySQL workloads in mid-2021, including a self-managed MySQL cluster with over 160 nodes in production, to AWS Graviton-based instances. To do this, Paytm had to first update its MySQL database to a minimum software version recommended for AWS Graviton processors, and because of the criticality of the databases as well as dependencies between workloads, this update was a complex undertaking. “The AWS teams supported us very well, especially considering the scale and speed at which Paytm works,” says Parakh Aggarwal, Director of Cloud Excellence and FinOps.

solution_components.name: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud
solution_components.role: Provides scalable compute capacity for application services or AI workloads.

solution_components.name: AWS Graviton processors
solution_components.role: Improve price performance for compute and database workloads.

solution_components.name: Amazon EMR
solution_components.role: Runs large-scale data processing and model training workloads.

business_outcome: Paytm continues to migrate its massive infrastructure to AWS Graviton-based Amazon EC2 instances (60% of EC2 migrated to Graviton as of Jan-2024) and expects to have 70 percent of its infrastructure migrated by mid-2024. Paytm plans to migrate all its 200-plus services to AWS Graviton eventually.
metrics: 30–35% cost savings on Amazon EMR workloads
60% of EC2 instances migrated to AWS Graviton
35% costs savings on overall compute costs
